explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem says a particular variable belongs to the free-variable set (`fv`) of a term built from the library's own definitions: `synCcompl`, `Class.cv` and `nb095AlphaDummy447/448`. The proof first uses the library lemmas `fv_syn_ccompl` and `fv_class_cv` to reduce this to membership in a singleton set. It then applies two generic Mathlib facts about finite sets: `Finset.mem_union`, so the variable only needs to be in one side of the union, and `Finset.mem_singleton_self`, which says an element belongs to its own singleton. These are routine glue and carry none of the theorem's content, which lies in the library's definitions of `fv` and its syntax. I did not search Mathlib beyond these two lemmas, since none of the theorem's constants exist there.
